title: Suarez closes the Roman locus: true proper latria of Christ's image with Christ—relative toward the image, absolute toward Christ
source_text: LXI. Denique Franciscus Suarez qui putat imaginem, cum exemplari, adorari posse uno & eodem adorationis actu, tam interno, quam externo, idque non abusive tantum, sed vere & proprie; consequenter etiam docet imaginem Christi, cum Christo ipso adorari posse vere & proprie adoratione latriae, cujus actus, qui sit unus atque indivisibilis, ad prototypum simul & imaginem terminetur. Neque tamen id pugnare putat cum Conciliis Ecclesiae Romanae, quae prohibent latriam deferri imaginibus, ut nec aliis ullis creaturis. Quoniam, quum imago Christi predicto modo adoratur, actus latriae per se primo tendit in Christum, in imaginem vero concomitanter tantum; licet autem creatura, ipsius judicio, non possit per se primo latria adorari, latria tamen coadorari potest: Sicut, inquit, purpura Regis coadoratur honore Regio. Addit eundem illum adorationis actum, quo adoratur Christus, & ipsius imago, esse respectu Christi, latriam absolutam, respectu vero imaginis latriam respectivam; quia honor ille Christo defertur, propter excellentiam quae in ipso est; imagini vero, propter excellentiam Christi, quem repraesentat. Nihil autem repugnare quin creatura latria adoretur, modo latria illa relativa sit, & non absoluta, id est, modo cultus ille creaturae deferatur, propter Deum, & non propter ipsam.
pass_a_gloss: Finally Franciscus Suarez, who thinks that the image can be adored with the exemplar by one and the same act of adoration, both internal and external, and that not only abusively but truly and properly; consequently also teaches that the image of Christ can be adored with Christ himself truly and properly with the adoration of latria, whose act, which is one and indivisible, is terminated in the prototype and the image together. Nor yet does he think that to conflict with the Councils of the Roman Church, which forbid latria to be deferred to images, as also not to any other creatures. Because, when the image of Christ is adored in the aforesaid manner, the act of latria tends per se first into Christ, but into the image only concomitantly; but although a creature, in his judgment, cannot per se first be adored with latria, yet it can be co-adored with latria: Just as, he says, the King's purple is co-adored with royal honor. He adds that that same act of adoration by which Christ and his image are adored is, with respect to Christ, absolute latria, but with respect to the image respective latria; because that honor is deferred to Christ on account of the excellence that is in him; but to the image on account of the excellence of Christ whom it represents. And that nothing prevents a creature from being adored with latria, provided that latria be relative and not absolute, that is, provided that cult be deferred to the creature on account of God, and not on account of itself.
pass_b_english: Suarez closes the Roman locus: one true proper latria-act can terminate on Christ and his image together.
Per se the act aims first at Christ; the image is only co-adored concomitantly—like royal purple with the king—so Councils forbidding creature-latria are not breached.
Toward Christ the act is absolute latria; toward the image, respective latria for God's sake, not the creature's.

lemmas.gloss: yet it can be co-adored with latria
